sections.h2: Where is Johnson County, Illinois, and what is it like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Johnson County lies in the far southern part of Illinois, the region known as Little Egypt, with Vienna as both its county seat and its largest city. It was organized in 1812 out of Randolph County and has 344 square miles of land. Williamson, Saline, Pope, Massac, Pulaski and Union counties surround it.

The 2020 census counted 13,308 residents, and every one of them was classed as living in a rural area. The state archives page notes that the county dropped township government in 1876, so its subdivisions are precincts: Bloomfield, Burnside, Cache, Elvira, Goreville, Grantsburg, Simpson, Tunnel Hill and Vienna. The Vienna Correctional Center, a state prison for men, shapes the county's age and sex profile in the census data.

Winters are mild, with Vienna's January lows averaging 25 degrees and July highs near 90. Rain falls all year, with May the wettest month at about 5.2 inches. A seller with an older roof or crawl space should expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at moisture.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Johnson County housing?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 13,363 residents as of July 2025 and 5,555 housing units. Among 4,101 households for 2020 to 2024, 82.0 percent own their home, one of the higher owner-occupied rates in southern Illinois. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $160,500, and median household income is $62,528.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,510, against $510 for owners without one. Median gross rent is $781, and the Census Bureau shows zero building permits issued in 2025, so new construction is thin. For a seller, that points to a small, local buyer pool where a clean title and paid tax bills help.

sections.h2: Which Johnson County offices should I call about property tax?
sections.html:
The County Clerk's site lists direct lines for the offices a seller needs. The Clerk and Recorder holds deed records back to 1815 and handles the recording of deeds and mortgages, plat books and delinquent taxes.

Johnson County offices and phone numbers listed by the County Clerk (source: Johnson County Clerk website)
OfficePhoneWhy a seller calls
Treasurer618-658-8042Bill amounts, payment, delinquent status
Assessor618-658-8010Assessment, exemptions, parcel questions
County Clerk and Recorder618-658-3611Recording a deed, delinquent tax records
Addressing618-658-5911Rural address questions

The Clerk's office is at 105 North 6th Street, Vienna, in the new courthouse and administration building, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to noon and 1 to 4 p.m., with after-hours appointments possible. The county commissioners meet on the second and fourth Tuesdays at 3:45 p.m. in the same building.

sections.h2: How does Johnson County bill and collect property tax?
sections.html:
The county runs an online property tax inquiry portal at johnsonil.devnetwedge.com, with separate searches for parcels and for mobile homes, plus a link to pay taxes. Search by parcel number, owner name or street address and print the record for your title company.

The county's own installment dates should come from the Treasurer's office, because they change from year to year and appear on each bill. State law sets the penalty: an installment unpaid after the later of June 1 or the due date printed on the bill is delinquent and bears 1 1/2 percent interest per month or part of a month in a county this size (35 ILCS 200/21-15). A payment mailed with a postmark on or before the due date is not late. The second installment follows the same rule against the later of September 1 or the bill date.

If a mortgage lender holds escrow and the tax goes delinquent through the lender's fault, the statute shifts the interest to the lender, so call the servicer first when a bill looks unpaid.

sections.h2: How does a Johnson County assessment work, and how do I contest it?
sections.html:
State law sets the assessment level outside Cook County at 33 1/3 percent of fair cash value, set each general assessment year as of January 1 (35 ILCS 200/9-155). Counties of this size publish the assessment list in a newspaper by December 31, and the notice must state the median level of assessment, the filing deadline and the homestead exemptions you may qualify for (35 ILCS 200/12-10).

To test your figure, divide the assessed value by the median level in the notice. If the result is higher than what the house would sell for, you may be over-assessed. A complaint goes in writing to the Board of Review within 30 calendar days of publication, and a complaint filed by mail counts on its postmark date (35 ILCS 200/16-55). If the Board's decision still looks wrong, a petition to the Property Tax Appeal Board is due within 30 days of the written notice (35 ILCS 200/16-160).

The Board of Review sits in the county courthouse. Call the Assessor at 618-658-8010 for the current filing address, forms and any board rules.

sections.h2: What homestead relief can a Johnson County owner claim?
sections.html:
The state code sets the amounts, and Johnson County falls in the group of counties that are not next to a county of 3,000,000 or more people. For 2023 and later years, that puts it in the lower tier of each exemption:

  • General homestead: the rise in equalized value above the 1977 figure, up to $6,000 (35 ILCS 200/15-175).
  • Senior citizens homestead: up to $5,000 for an owner 65 or older who is liable for the taxes (35 ILCS 200/15-170).
  • Senior owners can also qualify to defer taxes, and the assessor must tell exemption holders so.

The statute also says that when homestead property is sold in a county under 3,000,000, the exemption stays in effect for the rest of the assessment year of the sale, and the assessor may require the new owner to apply for the following year. A buyer should plan to file the paperwork early.

The Assessor can also tell you about disability, veteran and improvement exemptions, which have their own state forms. Ask which applications are due this cycle and whether a renewal is waiting.

sections.h2: What happens if Johnson County tax goes unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax is published as delinquent and can be offered at the annual tax sale, and the County Clerk's office lists delinquent taxes among its services. Under state law, property sold at a tax sale can generally be redeemed within 3 years of the sale date, with exceptions that depend on the property's status on the sale date (35 ILCS 200/21-350).

If your bill is behind, get a payoff figure with interest from the Treasurer, ask the Clerk whether any tax has been sold on the parcel, and give both numbers to the title company. Paying the balance at closing out of proceeds is common, but the contract should say so.

sections.h2: How should I prepare a Johnson County house for sale?
sections.html:
Find your parcel record on the inquiry portal and confirm the owner name matches your deed. If the deed is in a deceased relative's name, bring the Clerk's office the paperwork you will need to record a transfer. Check for unpaid mobile home tax if a manufactured home sits on the land, since the portal has its own mobile home search.

Pay or schedule the current installment, and ask your lender about escrow. Rural parcels may need a corrected address, so the Addressing line is worth a call. Finally, pull your last assessment notice so you can show a buyer what the assessor valued the property at.

faqs.q: When are Johnson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The Treasurer sets the installment dates, and they appear on each bill and change by year. Call 618-658-8042. State law treats an installment as delinquent after the later of June 1 or the printed due date, and the same for September 1 on the second.

faqs.q: What interest does Johnson County charge on late tax?
faqs.a: State law sets 1 1/2 percent per month or part of a month for counties of this size. A payment postmarked on or before the due date is not delinquent.

faqs.q: Where do I search Johnson County tax records online?
faqs.a: Use the county's property tax inquiry portal at johnsonil.devnetwedge.com. It has separate searches for parcels and mobile homes, and a link to pay.

faqs.q: How much is the general homestead exemption in Johnson County?
faqs.a: State law caps it at $6,000 of equalized assessed value for 2023 and later in counties that are not next to a county of 3,000,000 or more. The amount is the rise above the 1977 value, up to that cap.

faqs.q: Does the homestead exemption pass to a buyer in Johnson County?
faqs.a: For the rest of the assessment year of the sale, yes. The assessor may then require the new owner to apply for the next year, so a buyer should ask the Assessor at 618-658-8010.
